node_kinds.name: process
node_kinds.title: Process
node_kinds.description: A piece of work the business carries out; a process may contain smaller processes to any depth.

node_kinds.name: event
node_kinds.title: Event
node_kinds.description: Something that happens at a point in time and is recorded, such as an order being placed.

node_kinds.name: entity
node_kinds.title: Entity
node_kinds.description: A thing the business keeps information about, such as a customer, a product or a document.

node_kinds.name: state
node_kinds.title: State
node_kinds.description: A condition an entity can be in, such as pending, paid or shipped.

node_kinds.name: attribute
node_kinds.title: Attribute
node_kinds.description: One piece of information held about an entity, such as a price or a date.

node_kinds.name: rule
node_kinds.title: Rule
node_kinds.description: A policy or constraint that governs how a process may be carried out.

node_kinds.name: actor
node_kinds.title: Actor
node_kinds.description: A person, role, team or system that performs a process.

node_kinds.name: metric
node_kinds.title: Metric
node_kinds.description: A measured or computed number the business tracks.

node_kinds.name: goal
node_kinds.title: Goal
node_kinds.description: An outcome a process is meant to achieve.

node_kinds.name: physical_source
node_kinds.title: Physical source
node_kinds.description: A concrete place where one business's data actually lives, such as a table, an API or a file.

tiers.name: structure
tiers.description: The universal grammar every graph is built on and validated against.

tiers.name: substructure
tiers.description: A domain's shared graph of processes and data that every business in the domain inherits; it holds data, never code.

tiers.name: instance
tiers.description: One real business's graph, which realizes a domain's graph and adds its own physical sources.

tiers.name: pattern
tiers.description: A stored universal process pattern that a domain's top-level process specializes by reference.

tiers.name: data_object
tiers.description: A stored canonical data object that a domain entity specializes by reference.

process.name: contains
process.description: a process contains a sub-process (Q408: the only depth)
process.inverse_description: a sub-process is contained by its parent process

process.name: consumes
process.inverse_description: an input is read by a process

process.name: produces
process.inverse_description: an output is written by a process

process.name: performed_by
process.description: a process is performed by an actor

process.name: governed_by
process.description: a process is governed by a rule

process.name: emits
process.inverse_description: an event is emitted by a process

data.name: transitions_to
data.description: an event records a transition into a state, optionally from props.from_state (note §23-24)
data.inverse_description: a state is entered by the event that records the transition

data.name: has_state
data.inverse_description: a state belongs to an entity

kpi.name: computed_by
kpi.description: a metric is computed by ONE computation source whose props.kpi_ref names its KPI store record (Q413)
kpi.inverse_description: a computation source computes one metric

slots.name: goal
slots.description: What the process is for: the outcome it serves.

slots.name: trigger
slots.description: What starts the process: an event, a schedule or a request.

slots.name: input
slots.description: What the process reads or consumes.

slots.name: entity
slots.description: The business thing the process works on.

slots.name: current_state
slots.description: The state the thing is in before the process acts.

slots.name: actor
slots.description: Who or what carries out the process.

slots.name: rule
slots.description: The policy that governs how the process runs.

slots.name: constraint
slots.description: A limit the process must respect, such as time, cost or capacity.

slots.name: decision
slots.description: A choice the process makes between options.

slots.name: output
slots.description: What the process writes or produces.

slots.name: target_state
slots.description: The state the thing is in after the process acts.

slots.name: event
slots.description: What the process records as having happened.

slots.name: data
slots.description: The information the process needs or keeps.

slots.name: feedback
slots.description: How the outcome is measured and fed back to improve the process.

slot_levels.name: required
slot_levels.description: A process of this type must have the slot filled.

slot_levels.name: recommended
slot_levels.description: A process of this type should have the slot filled when the business knows it.

slot_levels.name: optional
slot_levels.description: The slot may be filled, and leaving it empty is not a gap.

slot_levels.name: not_applicable
slot_levels.description: The slot does not apply to a process of this type.

intents.name: describe
intents.description: what something is, holds or consists of

intents.name: how
intents.description: how something works or is carried out: its steps, actors and flow

intents.name: why
intents.description: why something happened or is so: causes, rules, upstream inputs

intents.name: decide
intents.description: which option to choose or whether to act, judged against rules and evidence

intents.name: calculate
intents.description: a number: a count, sum, average, minimum, maximum or grouping

intents.name: history
intents.description: what happened over time: events and state changes

intents.name: next
intents.description: what happens or should be done next: downstream effects and actions

attribute_categories.description: Long-lived information that defines an entity, such as a name or an address.
A value taken from a shared list, or a pointer to another entity.
Information recorded by one business transaction, such as an amount or a quantity.
A measured or computed number held about an entity.
Information recorded when something happened, such as a timestamp.

core_attribute_categories.description: A core object's long-lived defining information.
A core object's value from a shared list, or its pointer to another core object.
A core object's information recorded per transaction.
A core object's measured or computed number.

data_types.description: A number with a fractional part, such as a price.
A calendar date without a time of day.
A calendar date with a time of day.
One value from a fixed list of named options.

cardinalities.description: At most one related entity on the far side of a relationship.
Any number of related entities on the far side of a relationship.

physical_source_kinds.description: A service endpoint the data is fetched from.
A document such as a spreadsheet, a PDF or a web page.
A computed value whose formula, operation and inputs live in the KPI store.
A data file such as a CSV export.

transformations.description: Works out a value, a choice or a plan from inputs: calculates, compares, matches or assesses.
Grants a request or an item: authorises, accepts or signs it off.
Refuses a request or an item: rejects, denies or turns it down.
Assigns stock, staff, money or capacity to a demand: reserves, assigns or dispatches it.
Places work, a booking or a delivery in time: sequences, books or arranges it.
Captures, compiles or consolidates facts into a record: logs, registers or extracts them.
Moves goods, money or information to another party: sends, pays, delivers or notifies.
Makes or performs the offering or a work product: prepares, builds, serves or repairs.
Observes, inspects or counts against a standard: tests, monitors, audits or reconciles.
Changes something already in place: corrects, revises, reprices or replenishes it.

lifecycle_states.description: Not yet acted on or not yet in force: drafted, requested, submitted or awaiting review.
In force or in progress: started, confirmed, assigned, issued or live.
Accepted or authorised: agreed, signed, validated or passed.
Refused or failed: rejected, denied, disputed or failed a check.
Finished: done, closed, paid, delivered, recorded or resolved.
Ended without completing: cancelled, withdrawn, expired, superseded or written off.
An entity's standing condition rather than a stage of its lifecycle: in stock, below reorder point, on hold.

core_roles.name: offering
core_roles.description: what the business sells: a product, a service or a package

core_roles.name: customer
core_roles.description: the party the business sells to

core_roles.name: supplier
core_roles.description: the party the business buys from

core_roles.name: resource
core_roles.description: what the business holds and uses to deliver: stock, materials, equipment or capacity

structures.description: The universal default: every node kind, every registered edge kind and processes nested at most eight deep, with no process type table named.
The universal default with the governed process type table named; every founded domain is validated against it and pins it.
